data.narrative:
Latitude is a Series B-stage space and aerospace company that has raised €50M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of five private peers at the same or adjacent stage—including Sierra Space ($8.0B Series C), Cowboy Space Corporation ($2.0B Series B), Varda Space Industries ($1.5B Series C), Aalyria ($1.3B Series B), and Skyryse ($1.1B Series C)—alongside six public space and aerospace equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL, and one additional ticker).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the €50M raised as a base proxy and applying a typical 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $95M. Peer-median analysis across the five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.5B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied: while the Space & Aerospace sector shows a 26.4x median price-to-sales multiple across listed peers, Latitude's revenue is not disclosed. 

The two applicable methods produce a wide triangulated range: $81M (low), $798M (median), and $1.7B (high). The significant dispersion reflects structural uncertainty in early-stage space-tech valuations, where peer comparables span nearly two orders of magnitude. Stage-progression suggests more downside; peer-median suggests substantially higher valuation. Without disclosed revenue or clearer operational milestones, the median estimate ($798M) should be treated as indicative rather than precise.
